citation: Grimnes G, et al. Vitamin D, insulin secretion, sensitivity, and lipids: results from a case-control study and a randomized controlled trial using hyperglycemic clamp technique. Diabetes 2011;60:2748-2757.
protocol: Hyperglycaemic clamp: dextrose 200 mg/mL bolus 150 mg/kg i.v. then glucose infused to hold venous glucose at 10 mmol/L for about 3 h (glucose every 5 min); first-phase insulin AUC 0-10 min, AUC 120-180 min, M and ISI over the last hour.
population: 160 Norwegian adults aged 30-75 y without diabetes (108 low and 52 high serum 25(OH)D, mean age about 52-54, BMI about 26.5, 49% women); placebo arm of vitamin D RCT n=45.

reports.marker: glucose, insulin pre/post in placebo group

note: Hyperglycaemic clamp with first-phase and second-phase insulin areas in a population sample, not strictly healthy volunteers (people with diabetes excluded). Skewed values are median (5th-95th percentile), normal ones mean +/- SD; insulin in pmol/L.
